segments.arabic: [739] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة عن أبي بشر عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: انطلق النبي ﷺ في طائفة من أصحابه عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ وقد حيل بين الشياطين وبين خبر السماء وأرسلت عليهم الشهب فرجعت الشياطين إلى قومهم فقالوا مالكم فقالوا حيل بيننا وبين خبر السماء وأرسلت علينا الشهب قالوا ما حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء إلا شيء حدث فاضربوا مشارق الأرض ومغاربها فانظروا ما هذا الذي حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء فانصرف أولئك الذين توجهوا نحو تهامة إلى النبي ﷺ وهو بنخلة عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ وهو يصلي بأصحابه صلاة الفجر فلما سمعوا القرآن استمعوا له فقالوا هذا والله الذي حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء فهنالك حين رجعوا إلى قومهم فقالوا يا قومنا { إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا } فأنزل الله على نبيه ﷺ { قل أوحي إلي }
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz. The devils had been kept from the news of heaven, and shooting stars had been sent against them. The devils returned to their people, who said, “What is the matter with you?” They said, “We have been kept from the news of heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us.” They said, “Nothing has come between you and the news of heaven except something that has happened. Travel to the eastern and western parts of the earth, and see what it is that has come between you and the news of heaven.” Those who headed towards Tihamah came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was at Nakhlah, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz, and was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Quran, they listened to it and said, “By Allah, this is what has come between you and the news of heaven.” Then, when they returned to their people, they said, “Our people, ‘We have heard a wondrous Quran, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.’” Allah then revealed to His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Say: It has been revealed to me.”

segments.arabic: وإنما أوحي إليه قول الجن
segments.english: Only the words of the jinn were revealed to him.

notes: The digital narrator name سعد بن جبير is explicitly corrected to سعيد بن جبير on the agreement of both prints. The original remains retained. The selected you in the second news-of-heaven statement is also printed in both witnesses; it is not silently changed to us as in the English comparisons. Only the Quranic fragments actually present are translated. The closing statement about what was revealed remains separately marked.

segments.arabic: [740] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثنا أيوب عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: قرأ النبي ﷺ فيما أمر وسكت فيما أمر { وما كان ربك نسيا } { لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة }
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited where he was commanded and remained silent where he was commanded. “Your Lord is never forgetful.” “You have indeed had a good example in the Messenger of Allah.”

notes: The selected recited and remained silent are not expanded inside the hadith to specify kinds of prayer. Both Quranic fragments are retained without adding surrounding verses.

segments.arabic: [741] وقال عبيد الله عن ثابت عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: ‘Ubaydullah said, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: كان رجل من الأنصار يؤمهم في مسجد قباء وكان كلما افتتح سورة يقرأ بها لهم في الصلاة مما يقرأ به افتتح قل هوالله أحد حتى يفرغ منها ثم يقرأ سورة أخرى معها وكان يصنع ذلك في كل ركعة فكلمه أصحابه فقالوا إنك تفتتح بهذه السورة ثم لا ترى أنها تجزئك حتى تقرأ بأخرى فإما تقرأ بها وإما أن تدعها وتقرأ بأخرى، فقال: ما أنا بتاركها إن أحببتم أن أؤمكم بذلك فعلت وإن كرهتم تركتكم وكانوا يرون أنه من أفضلهم وكرهوا أن يؤمهم غيره فلما أتاهم النبي ﷺ أخبروه الخبر، فقال: يا فلان ما يمنعك أن تفعل ما يأمرك به أصحابك وما يحملك على لزوم هذه السورة في كل ركعة، فقال إني أحبها، فقال حبك إياها أدخلك الجنة
segments.english: A man of the Ansar used to lead them in prayer in the mosque of Quba’. Whenever he began a surah to recite for them during the prayer, he began with “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” until he finished it, then recited another surah with it. He did this in every rak‘ah. His companions spoke to him, saying, “You begin with this surah, then you do not consider it sufficient until you recite another. Either recite it, or leave it and recite another.” He said, “I will not leave it. If you would like me to lead you in prayer in this way, I will do so; and if you dislike it, I will leave you.” They considered him one of the best of them, and did not want anyone else to lead them. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to them, they told him what had happened. He said, “So-and-so, what prevents you from doing what your companions ask you to do, and what makes you persist in this surah in every rak‘ah?” He said, “I love it.” He said, “Your love for it has admitted you to the Garden.”

comparisons.note: The pinned EPUB goes directly from Ibn Abbas on reciting and remaining silent (1.12.741) to Abu Wail and the paired Mufassal surahs (1.12.742). The Quba imam report is absent in this checked adjacent sequence. Bewley 741 and both Arabic prints contain it. This is a local checked absence, not a claim about all English editions.

notes: The source begins Ubaydullah said, not related to us. The modern print expands his name and the historical print expands Anas’s name; neither expansion is inserted into the selected chain. Both prints support على لزوم where the digital source has عل لزوم; the correction is explicit. segments.arabic: [742] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن عمرو بن مرة قال: سمعت أبا وائل قال
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abu Wa’il say:

segments.arabic: جاء رجل إلى بن مسعود، فقال قرأت المفصل الليلة في ركعة، فقال هذا كهذ الشعر لقد عرفت النظائر التي كان النبي ﷺ يقرن بينهن فذكر عشرين سورة من المفصل سورتين في كل ركعة
segments.english: A man came to Ibn Mas‘ud and said, “I recited the Mufassal last night in one rak‘ah.” He said, “Rattling it off like poetry! I know the comparable surahs that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pair together.” He then mentioned twenty surahs of the Mufassal, two surahs in each rak‘ah.

notes: The printed vowel marks identify هذًّا كهذّ الشعر as rapid recitation like poetry. The selected and historical text have two surahs in each rakah; the modern print adds two from the Ha Mim group. That addition, also reflected in the Khan-family comparison, is documented rather than inserted.

segments.arabic: [743] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا همام عن يحيى عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان يقرأ في الظهر في الأوليين بأم الكتاب وسورتين وفي الركعتين الأخريين بأم الكتاب ويسمعنا الآية ويطول في الركعة الأولى مالا يطول في الركعة الثانية وهكذا في العصر وهكذا في الصبح
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Mother of the Book and two surahs in the first two rak‘ahs of the noon prayer, and the Mother of the Book in the last two rak‘ahs. He would make a verse audible to us, and prolong the first rak‘ah more than the second. It was likewise in the afternoon prayer, and likewise in the dawn prayer.

notes: The selected Mother of the Book designation remains. Sometimes is absent here and is not imported from either English comparison or report 745. The closing likewise statements remain without an explanation that could imply four rakahs for the dawn prayer.

segments.arabic: [744] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا جرير عن الأعمش عن عمارة بن عمير عن أبي معمر
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from Abu Ma‘mar:

segments.arabic: قلت لخباب أكان رسول الله ﷺ يقرأ في الظهر والعصر قال: نعم قلنا من أين علمت قال باضطراب لحيته
segments.english: I said to Khabbab, “Did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” He said, “Yes.” We said, “How did you know?” He said, “By the movement of his beard.”

notes: The selected singular I said followed by plural We said remains. The first question is not made plural as in the Khan-family comparison.

segments.arabic: [745] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف حدثنا الأوزاعي حدثني يحيى بن أبي كثير حدثني عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. Al-Awza‘i related to us. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to me. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah related to me, from his father:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان يقرأ بأم الكتاب وسورة معها في الركعتين الأوليين من صلاة الظهر وصلاة العصر ويسمعنا الآية أحيانا وكان يطيل في الركعة الأولى
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Mother of the Book and a surah with it in the first two rak‘ahs of the noon and afternoon prayers. Sometimes he would make a verse audible to us. He used to prolong the first rak‘ah.

notes: Both related to me verbs are retained. The source explicitly says sometimes here, unlike 743.

segments.arabic: [746] حدثنا أبو نعيم حدثنا هشام عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. Hisham related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان يطول في الركعة الأولى من صلاة الظهر ويقصر في الثانية ويفعل ذلك في صلاة الصبح
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to prolong the first rak‘ah of the noon prayer and shorten the second. He would do the same in the dawn prayer.

notes: Both prints include أبي in Yahya ibn Abi Kathir; the selected digital name omits it. The correction retains the original and cites both exact pages.

segments.arabic: [747] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن سعيد بن المسيب وأبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن أنهما أخبراه عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, who both informed him, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ قال: إذا أمن الإمام فأمنوا فإنه من وافق تأمينه تأمين الملائكة غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه،
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When the imam says Amin, say Amin, for whoever’s saying of Amin coincides with the angels’ saying of Amin will have his previous sins forgiven.”

segments.arabic: وقال ابن شهاب وكان رسول الله ﷺ يقول: آمين
segments.english: Ibn Shihab said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “Amin.”

notes: Both named transmitters and both informed him remain in the chain. The Ibn Shihab closing statement remains separately attributed, with its own honorific. The historical print says Messenger of Allah in the opening report; the selected and modern print say Prophet.

segments.arabic: [748] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إذا قال أحدكم آمين وقالت الملائكة في السماء آمين فوافقت إحداهما الأخرى غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When one of you says Amin and the angels in heaven say Amin, and one coincides with the other, his previous sins are forgiven.”

notes: The full selected chain and companion honorific remain. This complete report stays distinct from the neighbouring accounts.

segments.arabic: [749] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن سمي مولى أبي بكر عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إذا قال الإمام { غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } فقولوا آمين فإنه من وافق قوله قول الملائكة غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When the imam says, ‘Not those upon whom there is anger, nor those who have gone astray,’ say Amin, for whoever’s words coincide with the angels’ words will have his previous sins forgiven.”

segments.arabic: تابعه محمد بن عمرو عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ ونعيم المجمر عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Amr followed him in relating it, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; and Nu‘aym al-Mujmir, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him.

notes: The complete two closing routes remain, including Muhammad ibn Amr, which the Bewley comparison abbreviates away. The Khan-family body omits both routes and adds interpretive group names to the Quranic fragment; none of those additions enter the selected translation. Mawla is rendered freedman here; the source’s short Abu Bakr name is not expanded.

segments.arabic: [750] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا همام عن الأعلم وهو زياد عن الحسن عن أبي بكرة
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from al-A‘lam—who is Ziyad—from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah:

segments.arabic: أنه انتهى إلى النبي ﷺ وهو راكع فركع قبل أن يصل إلى الصف فذكر ذلك للنبي ﷺ، فقال زادك الله حرصا ولا تعد
segments.english: He reached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was bowing, and bowed before he reached the row. He mentioned this to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “May Allah increase your eagerness, but do not do it again.”

notes: The selected third-person narration and the identification al-Alam, who is Ziyad, remain. The wording is not expanded to identify exactly which action the last instruction concerns.

segments.arabic: [751] حدثنا إسحاق الواسطي قال: حدثنا خالد عن الجريري عن أبي العلاء عن مطرف عن عمران بن حصين قال
segments.english: Ishaq al-Wasiti related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-‘Ala’, from Mutarrif, from ‘Imran ibn Husayn, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى مع علي رضى الله تعالى عنه بالبصرة، فقال: ذكرنا هذا الرجل صلاة كنا نصليها مع رسول الله ﷺ فذكر أنه كان يكبر كلما رفع وكلما وضع
segments.english: He prayed with ‘Ali, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, in Basrah, and said, “This man has reminded us of a prayer we used to pray with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” He mentioned that he would say the takbir whenever he rose and whenever he lowered himself.

notes: The selected short narrator names are not expanded. The repeated whenever and third-person framing remain.

segments.arabic: [752] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أنه كان يصلي بهم فيكبر كلما خفض ورفع فإذا انصرف قال إني لأشبهكم صلاة برسول الله ﷺ
segments.english: He used to lead them in prayer, saying the takbir whenever he lowered himself or rose. When he finished, he said, “My prayer resembles the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more closely than that of any of you.”

notes: The complete chain remains. The selected them is not changed to us in order to follow the abbreviated Khan-family opening.

segments.arabic: [753] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد عن غيلان بن جرير عن مطرف بن عبد الله قال
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Mutarrif ibn ‘Abdullah, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت خلف علي بن أبي طالب رضى الله تعالى عنه أنا وعمران بن حصين فكان إذا سجد كبر وإذا رفع رأسه كبر وإذا نهض من الركعتين كبر فلما قضى الصلاة أخذ بيدي عمران بن حصين، فقال قد ذكرني هذا صلاة محمد ﷺ أو قال لقد صلى بنا صلاة محمد ﷺ
segments.english: ‘Imran ibn Husayn and I prayed behind ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. When he prostrated, he said the takbir; when he raised his head, he said the takbir; and when he rose after the two rak‘ahs, he said the takbir. When he finished the prayer, ‘Imran ibn Husayn took my hand and said, “This has reminded me of the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace”—or he said, “He has led us in the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: Both alternative closing formulations and both honorifics remain. The selected short Hammad name is not expanded from the historical print.

segments.arabic: [754] حدثنا عمرو بن عون قال: حدثنا هشيم عن أبي بشر عن عكرمة قال:
segments.english: ‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from ‘Ikrimah, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رجلا عند المقام يكبر في كل خفض ورفع وإذا قام وإذا وضع فأخبرت بن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال أو ليس تلك صلاة النبي ﷺ لا أم لك
segments.english: I saw a man at the Maqam saying the takbir at every lowering and rising, when he stood and when he lowered himself. I informed Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. He said, “Is that not the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? May you have no mother!”

notes: The full concluding Arabic expression remains in a literal working rendering, with Ibn Hajar’s explanation separately cited as context. The Khan-family body paraphrases it as admonished me. The source’s Maqam is not expanded inside the report.

segments.arabic: [755] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: أخبرنا همام عن قتادة عن عكرمة قال
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam informed us, from Qatadah, from ‘Ikrimah, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت خلف شيخ بمكة فكبر ثنتين وعشرين تكبيرة فقلت لابن عباس إنه أحمق، فقال ثكلتك أمك سنة أبي القاسم ﷺ،
segments.english: I prayed behind an old man in Makkah, and he said the takbir twenty-two times. I said to Ibn ‘Abbas, “He is foolish.” He said, “May your mother be bereaved of you! The practice of Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

segments.arabic: وقال موسى حدثنا أبان حدثنا قتادة حدثنا عكرمة
segments.english: Musa said: Aban related to us. Qatadah related to us. ‘Ikrimah related to us.

segments.arabic: [756] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني أبو بكر ابن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث أنه سمع أبا هريرة يقول
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah say:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا قام إلى الصلاة يكبر حين يقوم ثم يكبر حين يركع ثم يقول سمع الله لمن حمده حين يرفع صلبه من الركعة ثم يقول وهو قائم ربنا لك الحمد
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood for prayer, he would say the takbir as he stood, then say the takbir as he bowed. Then he would say, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” as he raised his back from bowing. Then, while standing, he would say, “Our Lord, to You belongs praise.”

segments.arabic: قال عبد الله ولك الحمد
segments.english: ‘Abdullah said: “And to You belongs praise.”

segments.arabic: ثم يكبر حين يهوي ثم يكبر حين يرفع رأسه ثم يكبر حين يسجد ثم يكبر حين يرفع رأسه ثم يفعل ذلك في الصلاة كلها حتى يقضيها ويكبر حين يقوم من الثنتين بعد الجلوس
segments.english: Then he would say the takbir as he went down, then say the takbir as he raised his head, then say the takbir as he prostrated, then say the takbir as he raised his head. He would then do this throughout the prayer until he completed it. He would say the takbir when he stood after the two rak‘ahs, after sitting.

segments.arabic: [757] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي يعفور قال: سمعت مصعب بن سعد يقول
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Ya‘fur, who said: I heard Mus‘ab ibn Sa‘d say:

segments.arabic: صليت إلى جنب أبي فطبقت بين كفي ثم وضعتهما بين فخذي فنهاني أبي، وقال كنا نفعله فنهينا عنه وأمرنا أن نضع أيدينا على الركب
segments.english: I prayed beside my father, pressed my palms together, then put them between my thighs. My father forbade me and said, “We used to do it, then we were forbidden to do it and commanded to put our hands on our knees.”

notes: The source says between my thighs, not the knees wording of the Khan-family comparison. The final passive statements do not explicitly name who forbade or commanded; a parenthetical attribution is not added.

segments.arabic: [758] حدثنا حفص بن عمر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن سليمان قال: سمعت زيد بن وهب قال
segments.english: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb say:

segments.arabic: رأى حذيفة رجلا لا يتم الركوع والسجود قال: ما صليت ولو مت مت على غير الفطرة التي فطر الله محمدا ﷺ
segments.english: Hudhayfah saw a man who did not complete the bowing and prostration. He said, “You have not prayed. If you were to die, you would die upon something other than the natural disposition with which Allah created Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: Fitrah is rendered natural disposition rather than being replaced with a legal judgment about another religion. The selected and modern print lack the historical print’s explicit عليها, and no Arabic word is silently added. This is Hudhayfah’s statement and retains its full selected chain.
